title: Blog front matter is parsed by gray-matter with its executable js engine left enabled
description: gray-matter 4 evaluates front matter that opens with a js or javascript language tag. A markdown file in content/blog with such front matter would run code on the build machine, which in CI runs with Pages deploy rights.
claimed_root_cause: matter() is called with default options, so the eval-based js engine is not disabled.

trace.description: matter(raw) parses front matter with default engines
The same default parse runs in the Vite config during build

blockers: Exploitation needs a merged contributor change, and the deploy workflow only runs on push to master, so impact depends on review and branch-protection policy that source does not show
No local execution was run because the sandbox rules cannot be enforced here

validation_plan.local: In an isolated sandbox with no network and a scratch copy, run matter() on a fixture whose front matter starts with a js tag that writes a marker file in scratch, and confirm whether it executes.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms master requires reviewed PRs. Fix: pass an engines option that throws for js and javascript, or reject non-yaml front matter, in all four call sites.

title: JSON-LD built with JSON.stringify does not escape the script terminator
description: A front matter value containing a closing script tag would end the JSON-LD block early.
claimed_root_cause: JSON.stringify output is placed in a script tag without escaping angle brackets.

trace.description: Repo-authored title, description and FAQ text
JSON.stringify output embedded in a script element

reason: Inputs are repo-authored front matter and locale data only, so no lower-trust principal reaches the sink. Kept as hardening.

title: Blog markdown renders raw HTML without sanitizing
description: marked runs with gfm only, so raw HTML and javascript: links in a post body reach the output.
claimed_root_cause: No sanitizer or html renderer override on the Marked instance.

trace.description: marked.parse output is embedded in the generated page

evidence.description: new Marked({ gfm: true }) with no sanitizer

reason: Only repository authors write this content, so there is no lower-trust principal and a review gate exists. A search of content found no script, iframe or javascript: strings. Kept as hardening.

title: GitHub Actions pinned by major tag with workflow-level pages and id-token write
description: First-party actions use floating v3 and v4 tags and every job inherits pages and id-token write.
claimed_root_cause: No SHA pinning and no job-level permission scoping.

trace.description: push to master and workflow_dispatch only

reason: Checklist deviation: only first-party actions, no pull_request trigger, no secrets and no attacker input crossing a boundary. Kept as hardening.

title: Root-URL locale redirect could be an open redirect
description: redirectToPreferredLang appends the current search and hash to a redirect target.

trace.description: Target is a fixed locale path plus search and hash

evidence.description: locales map supplies fixed path values; unknown saved values are ignored

reason: The target always begins with a fixed relative locale path, so the origin cannot change; search and hash stay on the same origin.

title: Vite dev-server advisories with a dev script bound to all interfaces
description: npm audit reports high advisories for vite and transitive build tools while the dev script uses --host 0.0.0.0.
claimed_root_cause: Vulnerable dev-server code reachable from the local network.
reason: The dev server is run only by the owner on a local machine, CI runs only the build, and no advisory covers code shipped to the browser. Transitive build-tool advisories need attacker-controlled inputs the build never receives. Fix by updating dependencies; filed as hardening.

title: Live GitHub Pages headers, HTTPS enforcement and repo settings are not visible in source
description: The site is served from GitHub Pages with a custom domain. Response headers (no CSP, no X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy), HTTPS enforcement and branch protection are platform settings that source does not show.
claimed_root_cause: Hosting-level controls live outside the repository, so their presence or absence cannot be established from source.

trace.description: Visitors reach getvoyagelog.app served by GitHub Pages
deploy-pages publishes dist with platform default headers

evidence.description: No CSP meta tag and no third-party loads; only first-party assets, so no injection sink is shown that a CSP would contain

blockers: GitHub Pages repository settings (Enforce HTTPS) and live response headers are outside source
No source-visible injection sink makes a missing CSP exploitable, so impact is unproven

validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks Settings > Pages shows Enforce HTTPS enabled and runs a HEAD request against the production host to record the headers; confirm branch protection on master. Treat the absence of CSP as hardening unless an injection sink is later added.
